answer: Anchor each agent identity in a bonded kernel: a newcomer locks a stake and must pass a chain of unpredictable, time-boxed verification tasks before it can trade. One honest agent pays this once; a tide of fakes must fund and staff every identity separately, so the cost multiplies with each clone. Reputation then accrues only to identities with a long, consistent history, like shale laid down layer by layer — a fresh clone starts with nothing. Forging a thousand credible identities costs a thousand stakes and a thousand task histories, far more than any one fake could earn back.
